title: Python Journey
summary: Five short lessons: print, variables, types, conditionals and loops. Each lesson types the target line, then makes it yours.

lessons.title: Hello, Qorix
lessons.summary: Your first Python statement prints a line of text.
lessons.coach: print() writes text to the screen. The text sits inside quotes.

exercise.title: Say hello
exercise.prompt: Type the line, then add a second print for Python itself.

hints.text: Type the line exactly. Ghost text shows the next character.
print is a function: the parentheses hold its input.
Quotes make this a string, not a variable.
Check the quotes and the closing parenthesis.
That is the whole program. Now add one more line.

freeform.prompt: Add a second line: print("Hello, Python!")
freeform.hint: Keep the first line. Add another print with its own text.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.summary: A name stores a value, and print() can show the value later.
lessons.coach: An assignment puts the value on the right into the name on the left.

exercise.title: Name and age
exercise.prompt: Type the assignment, then add age = 36 and two print lines.

hints.text: Type the assignment exactly. The equals sign is not a comparison here.
name is the label you choose. It is not text, so it has no quotes.
Ada is text, so it stays inside quotes.
Check the equals sign and both pairs of quotes.
The name now holds Ada. Reuse it in the printed greeting.

freeform.prompt: Add age = 36, then print("Hello, " + name) and print(name, "is", age).
freeform.example:
name = "Ada"
age = 36
print("Hello, " + name)
print(name, "is", age)
freeform.hint: Put age on its own line. The two print calls use the variables instead of repeating their values.

lessons.title: Types
lessons.summary: Numbers and text are different types, and type() names them.
lessons.coach: type(value) returns the kind of value: int, float or str.

exercise.title: Ask for the type
exercise.prompt: Type the three values, then print type(count), type(price) and type(label).

hints.text: Three lines, one value each. Decimals use a dot, not a comma.
3 has no decimal point, so Python stores it as an int.
2.5 has a decimal point, so Python stores it as a float.
Text in quotes is a str.
Check the decimal point and the quotes around coffee.
Now ask Python to report each type.

freeform.prompt: Print type(count), type(price) and type(label), one per line.
freeform.example:
count = 3
price = 2.5
label = "coffee"
print(type(count))
print(type(price))
print(type(label))
freeform.hint: Put each value inside type(), then give each result its own print line.

lessons.title: Conditionals
lessons.summary: if and else let a program choose which lines run.
lessons.coach: Python runs the indented block under if only when the condition is true.

exercise.title: Pass or retry
exercise.prompt: Type the if branch, then change score to 40 and add the else branch.

hints.text: The print line is indented by four spaces. Keep them.
>= means greater than or equal to. 75 satisfies it.
The indented line belongs to the if block.
Check the colon at the end of the if line and the four spaces before print.
The if branch works. Now make the other branch run.

freeform.prompt: Change score to 40. Add else: and print("retry") with the same indentation.
freeform.hint: else sits at the same level as if. Its print line is indented by four spaces.

lessons.title: Loops
lessons.summary: for repeats a block once for every value in a range.
lessons.coach: range(1, 6) produces 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. The stop value is not included.

exercise.title: Square numbers
exercise.prompt: Type the loop, then change print(number) to print(number * number).

hints.text: The print line inside the loop is indented by four spaces.
range(1, 6) stops before 6, so the loop runs five times.
number takes each value in turn.
Check the colon after the range and the four spaces before print.
The loop works. Now make it print squares instead.

freeform.prompt: Change the body to print(number * number). Keep the same range.
freeform.example:
for number in range(1, 6):
    print(number * number)
freeform.hint: Multiply number by itself inside print(). The indentation stays the same.
